heroHeadline: Sheinbaum at Day 573: U.S. DOJ Indicts Sinaloa Governor Rocha Moya — 'If No Clear Proof, This Is Political'; Mexico Q1 GDP Contracts -0.8%
heroSubtitle: April 30 brought two major shocks for the Sheinbaum administration. At the mañanera held on Día del Niño, the president responded forcefully to the U.S. Department of Justice's unprecedented April 29 indictment of Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya and nine officials on charges of conspiring with Los Chapitos to import narcotics — the first time a sitting Mexican governor has been charged by a foreign government. Sheinbaum declared: 'If there are no clear proofs, it is evident that the objective of these accusations is political. Under no circumstances will we allow the intrusion or interference of a foreign government in decisions that belong exclusively to the Mexican people.' She demanded 'irrefutable proof' before any extradition proceedings could begin, and tasked the FGR to investigate and advise the SRE. Mexico's Foreign Ministry issued a parallel statement that the extradition documents 'do not contain sufficient evidence.' The DOJ charges arrive on top of the ongoing CIA-Chihuahua sovereignty crisis, adding a second major US-Mexico confrontation. Also on April 30, INEGI released its preliminary Q1 2026 GDP estimate confirming a -0.8% quarterly contraction and only +0.2% annual growth — all three sectors (primary -1.4%, secondary -1.1%, tertiary -0.6%) declined. The contraction reflects $17.4 billion in lost investment due to U.S. tariff uncertainty and puts pressure on the government's full-year projection of 1.8–2.8%. Banxico, which signaled on April 28 that one final rate cut may come in May, faces a challenging dual mandate. The USMCA first official negotiating round remains scheduled for the week of May 25.
